children: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone shares gained over 1 percent in afternoon trade on September 2, bucking the sharp weakness in the broader market, after the company reported its highest-ever monthly cargo volumes for August.

The Adani Ports and SEZ stock was trading around Rs 1,666, up 1.1 percent, and was among the top Nifty 50 gainers. The outperformance came as the broader market remained under heavy selling pressure. At 12:20 pm, the Nifty 50 was down 235 points, or 0.98 percent, at 23,820.70, while the Sensex had fallen 653 points, or 0.85 percent, to 76,291.46.

Adani Ports handled a record 50 million metric tonnes (MMT) of cargo in August, marking its highest-ever monthly volume and an increase of 19 percent from a year earlier. The company attributed the performance to strong growth across its domestic and international port network.

Cargo growth during the month was broad-based, with dry cargo volumes rising 25 percent year-on-year and container volumes increasing 15 percent. For the year to date through August, Adani Ports handled 234.4 MMT of cargo, up 16 percent from the corresponding period last year. Dry cargo volumes during the period grew 17 percent, while container volumes increased 15 percent.

The company said growth in its container business was supported by the rapid expansion of its transshipment platform led by Vizhinjam and Colombo, which has helped it increase its share of regional trade flows. Adani Ports also highlighted a strengthening presence in liquid cargo and growing traction in dry cargo, including coastal cargo.
The latest monthly performance also keeps Adani Ports on course towards its longer-term ambition of handling 1 billion metric tonnes of annual cargo by FY31, the company said.

Meanwhile, logistics rail volumes stood at 54,131 twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) in August, up 6 percent sequentially. However, year-to-date rail volumes remained weak at 2.50 lakh TEUs, down 33 percent year-on-year.

Adani Ports shares have gained 12.4 percent so far in 2026, significantly outperforming the Nifty 50, which has declined 8.8 percent over the same period. At the current price, the ports and logistics major commands a market capitalisation of around Rs 3.84 lakh crore.

title: Adani Ports and SEZ shares rise over 1% as August cargo volumes hit record 50 MMT, jump 19% YoY
